title: Web Vitals & Measuring Performance
summary: **Core Web Vitals** quantify real user experience: **LCP** (loading), **CLS** (visual stability), **INP** (responsiveness). You optimize what you measure — with Lighthouse, the Performance panel, and field data.

subtopics.title: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)
subtopics.explanation: Time until the largest visible element renders — the loading metric. Improve with fast TTFB, preloading the hero image, and cutting render-blocking resources.

subtopics.title: CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)
subtopics.explanation: How much content jumps during load — visual stability. Reserve space for images/ads (width/height, aspect-ratio) and avoid inserting content above existing content.

subtopics.title: INP (Interaction to Next Paint)
subtopics.explanation: Responsiveness to user input — replaces FID. Improve by reducing long tasks, breaking up JS work, and keeping the main thread free.

subtopics.title: Lab vs field
subtopics.explanation: Lab tools (Lighthouse) are reproducible but synthetic; field data (RUM/CrUX) reflects real users. Optimize with lab, validate with field.

foundations.overview: Core Web Vitals are Google's user-centric performance metrics: LCP measures how fast the main content loads, CLS measures how much the layout jumps, and INP measures how responsive the page is to interactions. You measure them with Lighthouse and the Performance panel in the lab, and with real-user (field) data in production, then optimize the dominant problem — because you can only improve what you measure.
foundations.formalDefinition: A standardized set of field metrics (LCP, CLS, INP) plus the lab tools (Lighthouse, DevTools Performance) and field sources (CrUX/RUM) used to measure and improve perceived performance.
foundations.whyItMatters: Vitals correlate with engagement, conversion, and SEO ranking; they turn 'the site feels slow' into specific, fixable numbers, and they're a common performance-interview framework.
foundations.mentalModel: A restaurant review with three scores: how fast the food arrives (LCP), whether the table wobbles (CLS), and how quickly the waiter responds when you signal (INP).
foundations.browserPerspective: These are measured from real browser rendering and interaction timings; the browser exposes them via the Performance APIs.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Auditing a page with Lighthouse, fixing layout shift from images, splitting long tasks to improve INP, and tracking field vitals after a release.
foundations.businessImpact: Better vitals lift conversion and search ranking; regressions quietly cost revenue.
foundations.engineeringImpact: A shared metric vocabulary lets teams set performance budgets and catch regressions in CI.
foundations.performanceImpact: Each vital maps to concrete fixes: preload/compress for LCP, reserve space for CLS, reduce main-thread work for INP.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A good Lighthouse score means real users are fast.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Lighthouse is lab data on one simulated device; validate with field data (CrUX/RUM) from actual users.

commonMisconceptions.myth: INP is the same as FID.
commonMisconceptions.reality: INP replaced FID in 2024 and measures responsiveness across all interactions, not just the first input.

theory.question: What are the Core Web Vitals and how would you improve each?
theory.directAnswer: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — loading: improve TTFB, preload the hero image, and remove render-blocking CSS/JS. CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) — visual stability: reserve dimensions for images/embeds with width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid injecting content above existing content. INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — responsiveness: reduce long main-thread tasks, split or defer JS, and avoid heavy synchronous work on interaction. I'd measure with Lighthouse and the Performance panel in the lab, then confirm improvements with field data from real users.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: The three user-centric performance metrics and their fixes.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: Vitals are the standard performance framework and affect ranking and conversion.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: Each vital maps to a distinct cause (load, layout, main-thread) and fix.

theory.whyImportant: Knowing the metric-to-fix mapping shows real performance competence.

nestedTopics.title: Performance budgets
nestedTopics.explanation: Thresholds enforced in CI so a regression fails the build before shipping.

followUps.question: Lab score is green but users complain of jank — why?
followUps.answer: Lab runs on a simulated device/network; real users on slower devices or variable networks can see worse INP/LCP — always check field data.

keyTakeaways: Core Web Vitals: LCP (loading), CLS (stability), INP (responsiveness).
Optimize with lab tools (Lighthouse/DevTools), validate with field data (CrUX/RUM).
Reserve image/ad space (aspect-ratio) to kill layout shift.
Break up long tasks to improve INP responsiveness.
Set performance budgets so regressions are caught in CI.
